application.cv_markdown:
# Elina Turunen

Tampere, Finland | elina.turunen@mail.example | +358 00 000 0098

---

## Education

MSc Applied Physics, Tammerkoski University (formerly TTK), 2001

---

## Professional Experience

**Signal Processing Engineer**
Vireo Sensor Systems, Tampere (with periods at the Oulu facility)
2002 – present

- Core member of the audio and sensor signal processing group for over two decades, working across hearing-instrument products, medical-device sensor boards, and industrial sensor platforms
- Developed and maintained embedded DSP firmware in C for TI C5500-series processors, implementing real-time audio processing chains with hard latency constraints under 5 ms
- Carried out RF front-end characterisation and calibration for the company's wireless hearing-aid link receivers, using vector network analysers and conducted-emission test setups at the Tampere test facility
- Contributed signal-processing algorithms for Vireo's participation in an EORA Aurelia Auxiliary Instruments subcontract, processing telemetry from an airborne validation flight campaign over Northern Scandinavia
- Seconded to the Oulu office for eighteen months (2019–2020) for a customer integration project with a local medical-device OEM
- Finnish citizen, held a permanent Finnish employment contract throughout tenure

---

## Selected Projects

**Hearing-aid microphone array processing** (2016 – 2021)

Designed and implemented acoustic beamforming algorithms for hearing-aid microphone arrays, targeting a 4-element MEMS microphone array on a behind-the-ear form factor. Developed adaptive null-steering routines in C that ran on the hearing aid's low-power DSP, achieving approximately 8 dB of directional gain in cocktail-party noise conditions. The work involved array geometry optimisation, spatial filtering under stringent power and latency constraints, and extensive perceptual listening evaluation with audiologists.

**Production calibration toolchain** (2012 – present)

Built and maintained a Python-based production calibration pipeline that automates the characterisation of hearing-aid sensor boards on the manufacturing line. The toolchain runs nightly regression tests, interfaces with lab instruments over GPIB/VISA, and generates calibration certificates. Currently used by the production engineering team across two sites, maintained with unit tests and CI.

**Multi-site documentation programme** (2014 – 2018)

Drafted and maintained the engineering group's internal documentation in English — design review records, test protocols, and customer-facing integration guides — as Vireo's documentation language switched from Finnish to English in 2014 for international partner delivery.

---

## Skills

Signal processing (audio, sensor, industrial), embedded firmware (C, TI DSPs), production tooling (Python), sensor characterisation, medical-device regulatory awareness (INEC 60601), MATLAB
application.cover_letter_markdown:
After twenty-four years at Vireo Sensor Systems, I have been thinking carefully about where the next part of my career should go. The Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara is the first opening that has felt like a genuine fit for the kind of work I want to keep doing, and for the direction I want to move in.

My career at Vireo has been almost entirely in audio and sensor signal processing. Hearing instruments, medical-device sensor boards, and the calibration and test infrastructure that supports them. It has been steady, technically deep work, and I have valued the breadth it gave me. Over two decades I have gone from embedded firmware through production tooling to RF characterisation, and I contributed signal processing work for an EORA subcontract that involved an airborne instrument validation campaign. But Vireo is a smaller company now than it was ten years ago, and the range of projects has narrowed. I want to stay hands-on as an engineer, and I want to work on instruments and systems that push further than what I have been doing.

The reason I think this is a natural step rather than a stretch: my Applied Physics degree from Tammerkoski University gave me a strong grounding in electromagnetic theory, Fourier analysis, and statistical signal processing. Those are the foundations I have drawn on in every role since — the mathematics of sensor arrays, noise modelling, spectral estimation. The specific application domains have changed, but the underlying theory has not, and it is the theory side I find most rewarding. Kaikuvaara's work in remote-sensing instruments is a domain I have not worked in directly, but it sits on the same mathematical foundations, and I am comfortable that my depth of practical experience would transfer without a long ramp-up period.

I have also contributed to a few published articles and technical reports over the years, though I would describe my publication activity as modest and secondary to the hands-on engineering.

Practically, I am a Finnish citizen, I spent eighteen months at Vireo's Oulu office in 2019–2020 and know the city well. My notice period at Vireo is three months.

I do not have experience in remote sensing specifically. What I do have is a quarter-century of building, testing, and shipping signal processing systems in C and Python, working with RF hardware on a real test bench, and solving problems under real engineering constraints. That depth is what I would bring.

I would be glad to discuss this further.

Elina Turunen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
